title: Sing It Back
year_note: On the album I Am Not a Doctor (1998). First released as a single on 8 March 1999 (UK 45); the Boris Dlugosch remix reached UK 4 in September 1999.

notes.made: Róisín Murphy and Mark Brydon wrote it. The album version runs 4:24 and AllMusic called it a 'techno torch song'. For the single the band commissioned a Todd Terry mix, didn't like it, and had to talk Echo into releasing Boris Dlugosch's version instead; in exchange Murphy co-wrote and sang on Dlugosch's own single.
notes.context: Murphy and Brydon met at a Sheffield party in 1994, where her chat-up line ('Do you like my tight sweater?') became their first album title; the band name is the drugged milk in A Clockwork Orange. I Am Not a Doctor only reached 64 in the UK. The Dlugosch remix went to 4 in the UK and number 1 on the US dance club chart, with a Dawn Shadforth video of Murphy dancing alone in a metallic flapper dress.

listen_for.where: Murphy's vocal, all the way through the album version
listen_for.note: Sung as a torch song at a slow club tempo, which is the mood the panel wanted and the remix traded for a dancefloor.

leads_to.title: Never Enough
leads_to.why: The payback for the remix: Murphy's first credited appearance on the UK singles chart outside Moloko.

notes.unverified: I couldn't find production detail on the album version (gear, bass part), so there's only one listen note.

culture.title: The Boris Dlugosch remix
culture.line: The album version came out as a single on 8 March 1999 and reached 45 in the UK. Boris Dlugosch's remix climbed to 4 that September and topped the US Dance Club chart.
